newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australians support Asian immigration cuts - poll.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australians support Asian immigration cuts - poll.

text.p: Most Australians support calls to cut Asian immigration, a newspaper poll said on Tuesday, as a bitter debate over racism continued to threaten Canberra's relations with Asia.
The Sydney Morning Herald newspaper poll said almost two in three Australians wanted an immediate freeze on immigration and 53 percent wanted the proportion of Asian immigrants cut.
Only 36 percent agreed with current immigration levels from Asia, which account for more than one third of the 100,000 immigrants each year.

The poll was prompted by a divisive racism debate sparked by independent politician Pauline Hanson, who warned in September that Australia was in danger of being swamped by Asians and urged a halt to immigration.

Australia's conservative government sought to limit the fallout from the debate, reassuring its vital Asian trade partners that it condemned racism and remained committed to non-discrimminatory immigration.
Foreign Minister Alexander Downer, in an article in Thailand's The Nation newspaper on Monday, stressed Australia was a tolerant society and blamed the racism row on a minority.
"Our friends in the region need to see us through the hype and recognise that Australia is going forward, not backward," Downer wrote.

Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer is also explaining his government's opposition to racism during visits to India and Singapore, handing out copies of a joint parliamentary motion with the Labor opposition condemning racism and pledging commitment to an open and tolerant society.
While condemning racism, Prime Minister John Howard has refused to directly repudiate Hanson's controversial remarks and has publicly defended her right to free speech.
